definition: Name of the municipality or city.
basis_or_formula: N/A — identifier field.
source: barangay Python package (PSGC April 2026 release).

definition: Province the municipality belongs to. For the 34 highly urbanized cities (independent of any province), this is a pseudo-province in the form '<City Name> (Not a Province)' — a convention already used by the source package for Isabela City and extended by us to the other 33.
basis_or_formula: N/A — identifier field.
source: barangay Python package.

definition: Philippine administrative region (e.g. 'Region IV-A (CALABARZON)').
basis_or_formula: N/A — identifier field.
source: barangay Python package.

definition: PSA municipal income classification, 1st (highest) through 6th (lowest), based on average annual regular income.
basis_or_formula: Direct value from PSA's published classification.
source: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) PSGC publication, Q1 2026 release, via the yng-me/psgc GitHub package. 1,633/1,655 matched directly by (name, province) after fixing a footnote-marker parsing bug (PSA appends '*' to a handful of recently-reclassified LGUs, e.g. '4th*' — this broke exact-string matching and wrongly pushed 6 real municipalities into the synthetic fallback; fixed 2026-07-08 by stripping trailing non-alphanumeric characters before lookup). 22 municipalities have NO real PSA match at all and use a DETERMINISTIC HASH of the municipality name (fabricated, no relationship to reality): Manila's 14 historic districts (Binondo, Ermita, Quiapo, Tondo I/II, etc. — modeled as pseudo-municipalities by the barangay package, but PSA does not classify income below the municipality level; City of Manila as a whole DOES have a real classification) and 8 BARMM 'Special Geographic Area' barangays (same issue — sub-municipality entities with no PSA classification of their own). These 22 are structurally unresolvable, not a data-fetching gap — STILL FLAGGED as a data integrity issue; recommend NULL or explicit 'not applicable' rather than the current fabricated per-row value.

definition: 2024 census population estimate.
basis_or_formula: Direct value from PSA's published population figures.
source: PSA PSGC publication (2024 population), via yng-me/psgc. Same fix and same 22 structurally-unmatchable municipalities as income_class (identical PSA lookup, identical failure set) — see income_class note. Still flagged for those 22.

definition: GIS-calculated land area of the municipality in square kilometers. NOT the official PSA/DENR-published legal land area — see caveat below.
basis_or_formula: True geodesic (ellipsoid-based) area of the municipality's boundary polygon, computed via pyproj.Geod on the WGS84 ellipsoid directly (not a flat map projection, so it does not carry UTM-zone-style projection distortion).
source: Boundary polygons: geoBoundaries ADM3 (municipality-level), which cites NAMRIA/PSA/OCHA as its own boundary-line provenance — CC BY 3.0 IGO. The area VALUE itself is a geometric calculation we performed on those polygons, not a figure copied from any official PSA/DENR area table (PSA's own PSGC publication has no area column at all). CAVEAT: geoBoundaries' polygons are simplified/generalized for file size and visualization, not surveyed to legal/cadastral precision — official PSA figures are ultimately sourced from DENR-Land Management Bureau cadastral surveys, which follow legally defined (sometimes decades-old, decree-established) boundaries that don't perfectly match a generalized GIS shape. Spot checks against known official-ish figures showed deviations from ~5% (large flat/coastal cities, e.g. Quezon City, Davao City) up to ~20% (small/mountainous municipalities, e.g. Tayum and Bangued in Cordillera terrain, where ridge/valley simplification has the largest effect). Point-in-polygon matching (vs. name matching) correctly resolved 1,649/1,655 municipalities despite 114 duplicate shape names in the source data; 6 used nearest-polygon fallback. Treat area_km2 (and everything derived from it: pop_density_per_km2, pop_density_norm, and the 20% population weight inside geo_score) as a good relative/comparative signal across municipalities, not an authoritative absolute figure.

definition: Population density: population ÷ area_km2.
basis_or_formula: population / area_km2
source: Derived field — see population and area_km2 sources.

definition: Mean daily solar irradiance for the year, in kWh/m²/day.
basis_or_formula: Annual mean of ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR band 'surface_solar_radiation_downwards_sum' (originally J/m²/day, converted via ÷3,600,000) sampled at the municipality's real coordinates. Sampling is a 3-pass fallback: exact point → 11km buffer max → 25km buffer max (the buffer/max passes exist because ERA5-Land is masked over water and its coastal fringe pixels read artificially low, e.g. a lakeside point can read ~1.6 when the true value is ~5.0 a few km inland).
source: Google Earth Engine (GEE), dataset ECMWF/ERA5_LAND/DAILY_AGGR (Copernicus Climate Change Service, ERA5-Land reanalysis), year 2023. 1,624/1,655 (98.1%) municipalities have a real GEE value; the remaining ~31 (mostly remote islets with no ERA5-Land coverage even after all 3 sampling passes — Batanes, Kalayaan, Turtle Islands, etc.) use the mean of real GEE values for other municipalities in the same province as a substitute, not a random/hash value.

definition: Solar irradiance normalized to a 0–1 scale relative to all other municipalities in the dataset.
basis_or_formula: MinMaxScaler applied to solar_irradiance_kwh_m2_day across all 1,655 municipalities.
source: Derived field — see solar_irradiance_kwh_m2_day source.

definition: Income class converted to a numeric scale: 1st class = 6, 2nd = 5, 3rd = 4, 4th = 3, 5th = 2, 6th/special = 1.
basis_or_formula: Direct mapping from income_class.
source: Derived field — see income_class source.

definition: Population density normalized to a 0–1 scale relative to all other municipalities.
basis_or_formula: log1p(pop_density_per_km2), then MinMaxScaler across all 1,655 municipalities. The log1p step compresses the heavy right tail of the density distribution (a handful of very dense cities vs. a long rural tail) — without it, a single extreme outlier (e.g. a small dense city) pins nearly every other municipality's normalized score near zero, making population density contribute almost nothing to geo_score.
source: Derived field — see pop_density_per_km2 source.

definition: Composite geographic opportunity score, 0–1, combining solar potential, income level, and population density.
basis_or_formula: 0.35 × solar_norm + 0.45 × income_score_norm + 0.20 × pop_density_norm (income_score is itself MinMax-normalized 1–6 → 0–1 at scoring time). Computed once nationally and stored per municipality — does not change between pipeline runs unless the underlying solar/income/population/area inputs are recomputed.
source: Derived field — weights defined in config.py WEIGHTS. See component field sources above.

definition: Final ranking score for a municipality within a specific pipeline run, 0–1. Only populated for the 1,318 municipalities that ranked in their province's top 20 during a completed pipeline run — the remaining 337 have geo_score but no final_score (never received the web-intelligence + AI synthesis step).
basis_or_formula: 0.70 × geo_score + 0.30 × web_score.
source: Derived field — weights defined in config.py FINAL_GEO_WEIGHT / FINAL_WEB_WEIGHT. See geo_score and web_score.

definition: Local commercial/economic activity score, 0–1, derived from Google Places signals for the municipality.
basis_or_formula: 0.35 × business_density + 0.25 × price_signal + 0.25 × rating_signal + 0.15 × anchor_signal, where business_density = min(business_count/20, 1.0), price_signal = min(avg_price_level/4, 1.0), rating_signal = max((avg_rating-1)/4, 0), anchor_signal = min(commercial_anchors/5, 1.0).
source: Google Places API (New), Text Search — two queries per municipality: general 'businesses establishments' and 'shopping mall factory industrial warehouse commercial center'. Cached per (municipality, province) in the local database for 30 days (config WEB_INTEL_CACHE_TTL_DAYS) to avoid repeat billing.

definition: AI-assigned confidence tier for the assessment: HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.
basis_or_formula: Assigned by the LLM synthesis step based on geo_score, web signals, and the model's own knowledge of the specific place; not a fixed numeric threshold.
source: Xiaomi MiMo (mimo-v2.5-pro) via Anthropic-compatible gateway, called in agents/synthesis.py.

definition: 2–3 sentence narrative assessment of the municipality's solar installation potential, referencing real characteristics of the specific place.
basis_or_formula: LLM-generated, grounded in geo_score components, web intelligence signals, and the model's background knowledge of the municipality.
source: Xiaomi MiMo (mimo-v2.5-pro), agents/synthesis.py.

definition: One concrete, municipality-specific solar business opportunity identified by the AI (stored as a JSON-array-formatted string).
basis_or_formula: LLM-generated.
source: Xiaomi MiMo (mimo-v2.5-pro), agents/synthesis.py.

definition: One concrete, municipality-specific risk identified by the AI (stored as a JSON-array-formatted string).
basis_or_formula: LLM-generated.
source: Xiaomi MiMo (mimo-v2.5-pro), agents/synthesis.py.

definition: Latitude of the municipality's representative point (city/town center, not centroid of the full land area).
basis_or_formula: Geocoded, not computed.
source: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap), rate-limited to 1 request/sec, cached persistently in data/processed/municipality_coords.json. Fixed 2026-07-08: the geocoder query included the formal PSGC name ('City of Candon', 'City of Manila' as province, honorific prefixes like 'Pres.'/'Sen.') which OSM often doesn't index by, silently returning zero results for real, easily-mappable places — confirmed live and fixed by retrying with the 'City of ' prefix stripped, honorifics stripped, and (for the one Roman-numeral split name in the dataset, 'Tondo I/II') a direct override to 'Tondo'. Recovered real coordinates for 7 of 16 previously-fabricated municipalities. 9 remain on a hash-jittered province-centroid placeholder (fabricated, not real geocoded positions, visually indistinguishable from a real coordinate in this CSV): the same 8 BARMM Special Geographic Area barangays as income_class/population (couldn't be resolved under either their invented pseudo-province or the real neighboring province — not fully investigated case-by-case), plus one remaining name variant ('Don Victoriano Chiongbian') that would need an unsafe generic surname-truncation rule to fix automatically, deliberately left unfixed rather than risk corrupting other valid multi-word names elsewhere in the dataset. STILL FLAGGED for these 9; recommend NULL or an explicit is_geocoded flag.
